name: port-manager
title: Port Manager
description: Find open ports and close them
author: lucaschultz

commands.name: kill-listening-process
commands.title: Kill Process Listening on
commands.description: Kill the process listening on a given port

commands.name: named-ports
commands.title: Named Ports
commands.description: Name ports to make them easier to find in the open port list

preferences.name: primaryPortAction
preferences.title: Primary Port Action
preferences.description: Choose which action to perform when selecting an port.

commands.name: open-ports-menu-bar
commands.title: Open Ports in Menu Bar
commands.description: List open ports in menu bar

tools.name: kill-process-on-port
tools.title: Kill Process on Port
tools.description: Kill the process listening on a TCP port and verify that it exits
tools.instructions: Kill the process listening on a TCP port after the user confirms the action.

port.description: The TCP port number, from 1 to 65535.

tools.name: list-open-ports
tools.title: List Open Ports
tools.description: List TCP listeners with their ports, addresses, exposure, process details, and named port labels
tools.instructions: List the current TCP listeners, including the details shown by Open Ports and the menu bar.

port.description: Return only listeners on this TCP port. Omit to list every open port.

exposure.description: Return only listeners with this network exposure.

tools.name: kill-open-port-process
tools.title: Kill Open Port Process
tools.description: Kill a listed TCP listener by its PID, all processes with its name, or its parent; always pass the listener's PID
tools.instructions: Perform a kill action from Open Ports for a PID returned by list-open-ports.

pid.description: PID of the listening process from list-open-ports. For target "parent", pass the child's PID, not its parentPid.

target.description: Kill this process, every process with its name, or its parent.

signal.description: Use the configured kill signal by default, with SIGTERM for "ask", or override it when requested. Windows always uses taskkill.

tools.name: list-named-ports
tools.title: List Named Ports
tools.description: List saved names for TCP ports
tools.instructions: List every saved port name from the Named Ports command.

tools.name: create-named-port
tools.title: Create Named Port
tools.description: Save a name for a TCP port that does not have one yet
tools.instructions: Create a named port without replacing an existing saved name.

port.description: The TCP port to name, from 0 to 65535.

name.description: A nonempty name such as Next.js.

tools.name: update-named-port
tools.title: Update Named Port
tools.description: Change the saved name of an existing named TCP port
tools.instructions: Update the name of a port that is already saved in Named Ports.

port.description: The TCP port whose saved name should change.

tools.name: delete-named-port
tools.title: Delete Named Port
tools.description: Remove a saved TCP port name
tools.instructions: Delete a saved port name without killing its process.

port.description: The TCP port whose saved name should be removed.

preferences.name: killSignal
preferences.description: The signal used to kill the process on macOS. Windows always terminates with taskkill.
preferences.title: Kill Signal

ai.instructions:
Use list-open-ports to identify a listening process before killing by name or parent.
Pass that listening process's PID to kill-open-port-process, even when killing its parent.
Use kill-process-on-port for a direct request to kill a listener on a known port.
Report the tool's result accurately, including when a process survives a kill signal.

@port-manager Delete the saved name for port 3000
